events.title: Chernobyl Nuclear Disaster
events.description: Reactor No. 4 at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant near Pripyat, Ukrainian SSR, exploded during a safety test at 1:23 a.m., releasing large quantities of radioactive material across Europe.
events.significance: It was the worst nuclear power plant accident in history, leading to mass evacuations, long-term health and environmental consequences, and major changes in nuclear safety policy and Soviet transparency.

events.title: William Shakespeare Baptized
events.description: William Shakespeare was baptized at Holy Trinity Church in Stratford-upon-Avon, England, which is the earliest documented record of his existence. His exact birth date is unknown but traditionally given as April 23.
events.significance: Shakespeare became widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language, and his plays and poems shaped literature and theatre worldwide.

events.title: Bombing of Guernica
events.description: German Luftwaffe's Condor Legion and Italian aircraft, supporting Nationalist forces in the Spanish Civil War, bombed the Basque town of Guernica, causing heavy civilian casualties and destruction.
events.significance: The attack became a symbol of the horrors of aerial bombardment of civilians and inspired Pablo Picasso's famous painting Guernica.

events.title: John Wilkes Booth Killed
events.description: Twelve days after assassinating President Abraham Lincoln, John Wilkes Booth was tracked down and shot by Union soldiers at a farm near Port Royal, Virginia.
events.significance: His death ended the manhunt for Lincoln's assassin and closed a dramatic chapter at the end of the American Civil War.

events.title: Tanganyika and Zanzibar Unite to Form Tanzania
events.description: The sovereign states of Tanganyika and Zanzibar merged to form the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, which was renamed Tanzania later that year.
events.significance: The union created a new East African nation that remains one of the few successful post-colonial mergers of states in Africa.
